claims.claim: Reviewers report that the game lacks direction or guidance, leaving players without clear explanations of what to do or how to play.

citations.review_text:
Played the Gamepass version. It was fun but felt like it lacks any kind of direction or story, and feels much lonelier than similar games like Terraria. Occasionally would crash. Had a weird sound issue where every sound was glitched and corrupted that required me to lower my sound output from studio quality to cd quality to fix, so its obvious this game wasnt made on a good engine- though not unexpected for an indie game

Overall once the novelty wears off everything becomes repetitive, boring, and monotonous- and for that reason alone, this game should be skipped

If the devs added NPCs, story, quests, and Steam Workshop- this could be a thumbs up
I had no idea what to do, to be honest
no idea how to play and the game does not help

I don't know if it was the seed, but firing up the game I couldn't see nothing, was in a claustrophobic room, and had to figure it all out before I die of hunger. Within the first 5 minutes my inventory was already full, and still no idea what does what, what to do or where to go. Still in a claustrophobic room with no light. 

On paper, I'd have liked the game. A beautiful crafting game with lots of possibilities for your creativity. In reality, I couldn't enjoy the game's subtle but very present urge to organise your surrounding so quickly, before you even know what button does what on your controller.

My first gameplay was through all the standard settings, not hard mode nor easy mode. I guess I could have tried the easier modes to see if anything would be better.

cohorts.summary: Mid-game transitions into automation tools and farming systems alongside grindy resource gathering, harsh enemy damage, and technical instability.

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the mid-to-end game phases and resource gathering as repetitive and grindy.

citations.review_text:
Core Keeper is one of those games I constantly find myself comparing to Terraria, and I mean that as a huge compliment considering Terraria is one of my favorite games ever.

The easiest way I can describe it is basically **2.5D Terraria**. :D

You start with almost nothing, explore further and further out, discover new biomes, gather better materials, upgrade your gear, fight bosses and slowly turn your tiny starting area into a massive base. That whole progression loop scratches the same itch Terraria does for me.

I especially love the exploration. Digging through a wall and suddenly finding some huge structure, new biome or completely unexpected area never really gets old. Then you have farming, fishing, building, automation, railways, tons of equipment and little secrets scattered around the world.

But despite the comparison, **Core Keeper still feels like its own game** rather than just Terraria from another perspective.

The combat and bosses aren't quite as deep as Terraria and some parts can get repetitive or grindy, especially later on, but the overall gameplay loop is just really satisfying.

Explore → find shiny thing → upgrade → kill boss → explore even farther.

My brain likes this.

**If you enjoy Terraria, survival crafting and games with constant progression, Core Keeper is extremely easy to recommend. :3**

I think the game isnt bad at all, but with how great it starts the mid to end game gets kinda repetitive, grindy and frustrating if through countless buffs, strong enemies still 1 or 2 shot you, you're forced to manually tend to all your crops and you're forced to make giant ass conveyor belts that transport ores directly into your base.

It has charming low resolution pixel art graphics, the quality of it astonished me multiple times, a skill and leveling system in wich doing specific actions like mining gives exp for that proffesion, basebuilding with farming, husbandry and a need to build npc housing like in terraria, a plothera of boss fights, ways to build your character and just tons of content, but as i already mentioned game feels very grindy if you wanna make use of everything it has to offer like potions, good food and production lines, while the bosses get mechanics that repeat over different bosses, to the point some bosses just feel like reskins with scaled life and damage.

Even though it feels like i talked more about the bad than the good in the game, i still think its a great game and its worth the price they ask, i would recommend this game to anyone thats searching for something that scratches that terraria itch.

Update: i see that theres a lot more automatization in the game, good for them, it was sorely needed and removes one of my main complaints, the constant grind you werent able to automize

claims.claim: Reviewers mention that certain character classes like summoner and mage feel underdeveloped or shallow compared to other options.

citations.review_text:
Really fun game. its not really super comparable to any existing games. the closest comparison is if terraria met stardew valley met factorio which the fact i had to use 3 games just shows how unique this game is. the skill trees are done very well and dont feel like a grind but are just something you will do throughout the playthrough. getting new gear can be a bit grindy but other than that not too grindy. 

fishing is nice and relaxing and has a very cool minigame you can enable in settings.
the classes are very cool but mage and summoner are still a bit shallow. if you do want to stick to one class this is a bit of a wiki game but if you arent picky with classes its very easily to find out what to do next while still being really rewarding to explore with how many unique structures and sub biomes there are

Boss fights are very nice. simple but still rewarding to fight. as of this review i have not gotten to the new biome added in the 1.2 update but im excited to see what it has to offer.

visually speaking core keeper is beautiful with the pixel art style and the stunning godrays and water physics. the textures feel detailed enough for you to get immersed but dont feel super noisy unlike alot of newer pixel style games.

this is such a fun game both solo and with friends and even if you dont like survival games do give core keeper a chance. Dev team you all cooked so hard and make a masterpiece. keep up the great work

Core Keeper is best described as a mix of Terraria and Stardew Valley with RPG elements.
The core Gameplay is well made and entertaining. Having a skill system with which you level certain skills with certain tasks feels rewarding especially since skills like cooking or gardening can unlock perks that help in fights.
The bosses in this game are more a hit or miss for me. Some are well made and fun to fight and then you have some that are either halfway out of your screen the whole time or feel like a bullet hell.
Core Keeper starts out very strong but the more you progress through the story and biomes the more it all starts to feel less fun and more grindy.
You can play certain classes of which I chose to play a summoner only to notice halfway through that this also forces me to focus on using magic. Both feel kind of underdeveloped and feel like they need a rework while newer classes and equipment feel much stronger and easier to use.
The Biomes at the beginning feel really good but the last 2 Biomes are very frustrating due to the enemy mass.

Core Keeper can be fun especially with friends but the last few hours can be exhausting

Core Keeper is a solid game with a very enjoyable progression cycle. I liked the transition from manual resource gathering to establishing basic automation for your base. The boss variety is also surprisingly high; there are so many bosses that it sometimes feels like a boss-fighting game. It's not a masterpiece, but if you enjoy base building, setting up automated systems, and fighting lots of bosses, it's definitely worth your time.

Best tip: don't worry about your starting class, you're not locked into one and will play parts of them all if you want to get strong.

I had this game on Switch first and got the Steam version to play with friends on their PCs, so my playtime overall is 270 hours. This is potentially the best game of the sanbox genre. Incorporates all the elements you want in exploring, mining, crafting, farming, cooking, fighting, hunting, and adds its own completely unique aspects. I'm not drawn to electricity in any game personally, but the builds my friends have done are incredible, so if you do like machines and automation you'll enjoy it here.

The music is absolutely beautiful across the whole game and the atmosphere is perfectly developed. The pixel art is great and the amount of items, weapons and armour is massive. The cooking system is really clever and I love the crop and fish diversity. I love the feature of using one outfit cosmetically without it affecting your actual armour build. The customisation opportunities are pretty limitless with what you can paint and design, each environment has its own fully realised characterisation too. 

Super replayable, I've gone through 5 different worlds with friends and by myself and have never gotten bored or felt like I wasn't being challenged once I'd understood how the game worked. It really just got more fun over time. I like how you're encouraged to try different builds with the overarching levels system and that your character isn't linked exclusively to one world and vice-versa, so if you feel too OP or like you want to run through things quicker you can change your character to a previous or new one.

The quality of life decisions are just so good, and the updates always deliver major improvements I didn't even know I wanted. The pouch system is a lifesaver for big expeditions. The fights are interesting and the way enemy spwaning works is excellent for when you want to clear an area or leave it natural, especially in the…

citations.review_text:
My friends and I have done 3 playthroughs of this game. Easily one of the most fun times we've had. From theory crafting builds, exploring, redecorating, setting up automatic farms on the base and some sessions were just grinding out resources with verry little progression. Core Keeper is my favorite sandbox game. The game wants you to explore it to find new scenes and resources. You really get to take in the world that you're in instead of it being a backdrop for whatever task you're trying to bulldoze through and that's what I really love about it. You get comfy in your base whether its a medieval town, a humble farm or a horizontal replica of a Terraria slum. Which in turn is what also makes it sad when you get to the end of your journey and what excites you when a new update drops. You get to explore new areas or test out new items and grow your world a bit more each time. 
Now it does have problems. I found it crazy how difficult the new mobs were in the Void and Voltage update compared to the bosses. Some of the grinds are ridiculous like getting the full fishing armor or the Sentry armor set. But there was a lot of fun to be had with those too. Sitting in call asking for help with a room of new enemies or going on a spontaneous fishing trip at 2 in the morning because someone needed Litho Trilobites for a build they didn't even use add to the fun as well. I hope to see more out of this game especially since they left the end of the last update with [REDACTED FOR SPOILERS]. Core Keeper is an easy recommend for me. Either with friends or by yourself, its a wonderful journey.

Core Keeper is probably in my top ten favorite games! The best way I could describe it is if Terraria and Stardew Valley had a child. It may give off the vibe of being wiki dependent like the two, but this game can very easily be completed without ever consulting a wiki. The Core basically tells you what to do and where to go next to progress the story which is very helpful. I only ever checked the wiki because I wanted to 100% the achievements. I played the game at its original release and its amazing to see how much it has expanded and will continue to receive huge content updates, definitely invest in this one!

However this game does suffer from some poor balancing issues imo. I found every single boss to be a cake walk that can be done in one try (apart from [spoiler] Igneous [/spoiler] lol). It is quite a shame because every boss you encounter seems like they [i] should [/i] be insanely powerful, but end up being wimpy. I found myself dying more to basic mobs throughout the entire game rather than the bosses.

END GAME SPOILERS:
[spoiler] At the time of this review, Breakers Reach is the final area of the game and it is pretty flawed. The mobs have an INSANE amount of health and do WAY too much damage, why do tiny metal crabs deal so much damage?? The jump in difficulty caught me way off guard, but it gave me hope that S.A.H.A.B.A.R and Oblidra may actually present a challenge. So imagine my disappointment when I was able to first try both of them in only like 20-30 seconds... I died more times in Breakers Reach than anywhere else in the whole game because of the mobs in that area. [/spoiler]
[spoiler] Also, discovering The Passage for the first time is one of the coolest moments in the game, and I think its one of my favorite areas. The vibes are really creepy and give the feeling that you shouldn't be there which I always find thrilling. I guess its supposed to be more of a barren wasteland type of area, but it would be really nice to see more content added …
